questions.q: The angle between two linear transmembrane domains is defined by following vectors $\mathbf{a}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ and $\mathbf{b}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
questions.solution:
The angle between two vectors is given by
$\begin{array}{rlrl} & \cos \theta & =\frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{a b}=\frac{1-1-1}{\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3}} \\ \Rightarrow & \cos \theta & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ & \therefore & \theta & =\cos ^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block is kept on the floor of an elevator at rest. The elevator starts descending with an acceleration of $12 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. Find the displacement of the block during the first 0.2 s after the start. (Take, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
The acceleration (downward) of the elevator is $12 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ which is greater than gravitational acceleration $g$. So, the block will act as a freely falling body.
From the motion of the block
$\begin{aligned} s & =u t+\frac{1}{2} g t^2 \\ & =0 \times t+\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times(0.2)^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 0.2 \times 0.2 \\ & =20 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: One end of a massless spring of constant $100 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$ and natural length 0.5 m is fixed and the other end is connected to a particle of mass 0.5 kg lying on a frictionless horizontal table. The spring remains horizontal. If the mass is made to rotate at angular velocity of $2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$, then elongation of spring is
questions.solution:
For the circular motion acceleration towards the centre is $\frac{v^2}{r}$. The horizontal force on the particle is due to the spring and $k l$, where $l$ is the elongation and $k$ is spring constant of spring.
$\begin{aligned} & k l=\frac{m v^2}{r} & =m \omega^2 r=m \omega^2\left(l_0+l\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad & \left(k-m \omega^2\right) l & =m \omega^2 l_0 \\ \Rightarrow & l & =\frac{m \omega^2 l_0}{k-m \omega^2}\end{aligned}$
Putting the values $1=\frac{0.5 \times 4 \times 0.5}{100-0.5 \times 4}=\frac{1}{98} \mathrm{~m}=1 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: A block of mass 2 kg is pushed against a rough vertical wall with a force of 40 N , coefficient of static friction being 0.5. Another horizontal force of 15 N , is applied on the block in a direction parallel to the wall. If the block will move, then its direction would be
questions.solution:
The net force $=\sqrt{20^2+15^2}-0.5 \times 40\begin{aligned} & =25-20=5 \mathrm{~N} \\ & \therefore \quad \tan \theta=\frac{20}{15}=\frac{4}{3} \\ & \therefore \quad \theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)=53^{\circ} \\ & \end{aligned}$
So, the block will move at an angle $53^{\circ}$ with the 15 N force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block slides down on an incline of angle $30^{\circ}$ with an acceleration $\frac{g}{4}$. Find the kinetic friction coefficient.
questions.solution: Consider the situation Let the mass of block be $m$. The equation of forces $\begin{aligned} m g \sin 30^{\circ}-f & =\frac{m g}{4} \\ f & =\frac{m g}{4}\end{aligned}$ Also, $N=m g \cos 30^{\circ}=m g \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ As the block is slipping on the incline, friction is $\begin{aligned} \mu_n & =\frac{F}{N}=\frac{m g}{4 m g \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\ & =\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle slides on surface of a fixed smooth sphere starting from topmost point. The angle rotated by the radius through the particle, when it leaves contact with the sphere, is
questions.solution: See the diagram Let the velocity be $v$ when the body leaves the surface. From free body diagram, $\frac{m v^2}{R}=m g \cos \theta$. $\Rightarrow \quad v^2=R g \cos \theta$ ...(i) Again from work energy principle, change in $\mathrm{KE}=$ work done $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m v^2-0=m g[R-R \cos \theta]v^2=2 g R(1-\cos \theta)$ ...(ii) From Eqs. (i) and (ii) $\begin{aligned} R g \cos \theta & =2 g R(1-\cos \theta) \\ 3 g R \cos \theta & =2 g R \\ \Rightarrow \quad \cos \theta & =\frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow \theta=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are connected by a spring of spring constant $k$. The block of mass $m_2$ is given a sharp empulse so that it acquires a velocity $v_0$ towards right. Find the maximum elongation that the spring will suffer.
questions.solution:
The velocity of centre of mass
$v_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{m_1 v_1+m_2 v_2}{m_1+m_2}$
When $v_1=0$ and $v_2=v_0$, then
$v_{c m}=\frac{m_2 v_0}{m_1+m_2}$
Now, let $x$ be the elongation in the spring.
Change in potential energy $=$ potential energy stored in spring
$\begin{gathered}
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{2} m_2 v_0^2-\frac{1}{2}\left(m_1+m_2\right) \\
\left(\frac{m_2 V_0}{m_1+m_2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{2} k x^2
\end{gathered}$
This gives, $x=\left(\frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1+m_2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} v_0$

questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: The density of a rod having length $l$ varies as $\rho=c+d x$, where $x$ is the distance from the left end. The centre of mass is
questions.solution:
Let the cross-sectional area is $\alpha$. The mass of an element of length $d x$ located at a distance $x$ away from the left end is $(C+D x) \alpha d x$. The $x$-coordinate of the centre of mass is given by
$X_{c m}=\frac{\int x d m}{\int d m}\begin{aligned}= & \frac{\int_0^1 x(C+D x) \alpha d x}{\int_0^1(C+D x) \alpha d x} \\ = & \frac{C \frac{l^2}{2}+\frac{D l^3}{3}}{C l+\frac{D l^2}{2}}=\frac{3 C l+2 D l^2}{3(2 C+D l)}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: A ball of mass $m$ hits the floor with a speed $v$ making an angle of incidence $\theta$ with the normal. The coefficient of restitution is $e$. The speed of reflected ball and the angle of reflection of the ball will be
questions.solution:
The parallel component of velocity of the ball remains unchanged. This gives
$v^{\prime} \sin \theta^{\prime}=v \sin \theta$ ...(i)
For the components normal to the floor, the velocity of separation $=v^{\prime} \cos \theta^{\prime}$
and the velocity of approach $=v \cos \theta$
Hence, $\quad v^{\prime} \cos \theta^{\prime}=e v \cos \theta$ ... (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii)
$\begin{aligned} v^{\prime} & =v \sqrt{\sin ^2 \theta+e^2 \cos ^2 \theta} \\ \text { and } \quad \tan \theta^{\prime} & =\frac{\tan \theta}{e}\end{aligned}$
For elastic collision, $e=1$, so that $\theta^{\prime}=\theta$ and $v^{\prime}=v$

questions.q: A tangential force acting on the top of sphere of mass $m$ kept on a rough horizontal place as shown in figure. If the sphere rolls without slipping, then the acceleration with which the centre of sphere moves, is
questions.solution:

From Eqs. (i) and (ii)
$2 F=\frac{7}{5} m a \Rightarrow a=\frac{10 F}{7 m}$

questions.q: A solid sphere is set into motion on a rough horizontal surface with a linear speed $v$ in the forward direction and an angular speed $\frac{V}{R}$ in the anticlockwise direction as shown in figure. Find the linear speed of the sphere when it stops rotating and $\omega=\frac{V}{R}$.
questions.solution:
If we take moment at $A$, then extemal torque will be zero. Therefore, the initial angular momentum = the angular momentum after rotation stop (i.e. only linear velocity exist)
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & M v \times R-\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) I \omega & =M v_0 \times R \\ \Rightarrow & M v R-\frac{2}{5} M R^2 \times \frac{V}{R} & =M v_0 R \\ \Rightarrow & v_0 & =\frac{3 v}{5}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A uniform ring of mass $m$ and radius $a$ is placed directly above a uniform sphere of mass $M$ and of equal to radius. The centre of the ring is at a distance $\sqrt{3} a$ from the centre of the sphere. The gravitational force $(F)$ exerted by the sphere on the ring is

questions.q: What is the change in the volume of 1.0 L kerosene, when it is subjected to an extra pressure of $2.0 \times 10^5 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$ from the following data? Density of kerosene $=800 \mathrm{~kg}\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ and speed of sound in kerosene $=1330 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The lower end of capillary tube is immresed in mercury. The level of mercury in the tube is found to be 2 cm below the outer level. If the same tube is immersed in water, upto what height will the water rise in the capillary?
questions.solution:
Given data:
Level of mercury in the tube is, \(\mathrm{h}^{\prime}=2 \mathrm{~cm}\).
Level of mercury in the tube is given as:
\(\mathrm{h}^{\prime}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}^{\prime} \cos \theta^{\prime}}{\mathrm{r} \rho^{\prime} \mathrm{g}} . \quad \ldots (1)\)
where \(\rho^{\prime}\) is the density of mercury.
Level of water in the tube is given as:
\(\mathrm{h}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T} \cos \theta}{\mathrm{r} \rho \mathrm{g}} \quad \ldots (2)\)
where \(\rho\) is the density of water.
Here, the same capillary is immersed in both the liquids hence, the radius of the capillary is same i.e. \(r\)
Using the standard values for variables and taking \(\theta^{\prime}=135^{\circ}\), in equation (1) gives:
\(\begin{aligned}
& 2=\frac{2(484.5) \cos 135^{\circ}}{r(13.6)(980)} \\
& r=\frac{685.083}{(26656)} \\
& r=0.025 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)
Using value of \(r\) and \(\theta=0^{\circ}\) in equation (2), gives:
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{h}=\frac{2(72.7) \cos ^{\circ}}{(0.025)(1)(980)} \\
& \mathrm{h}=\frac{145.4}{(24.5)} \\
& \mathrm{h}=5.9 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Water level is maintained in a cylindrical vessel upto a fixed height $H$. The vessel is kept on a horizontal plane. At what height above the bottom should a hole be made in the vessel, so that the water stream coming out of the hole strikes the horizontal plane of the greatest distance from the vessel?
questions.solution:
The velocity with which water will came out
$v=\sqrt{2 g(H-h)}$
The time of flight of water ejected from the hole.
$\begin{aligned} t & =\sqrt{\frac{2 h}{g}}=\text { time of flight } \\ \therefore \quad x & =v \times t \\ & =\sqrt{2 g(H-h)} \times \sqrt{\frac{2 h}{g}}=\sqrt{4\left(H h-h^2\right)}\end{aligned}$
For $x$ to be maximum
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d x}{d h}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & d \frac{\sqrt{4\left(H h-h^2\right)}}{d h}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 0=H-2 h \Rightarrow h=\frac{H}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The earth receives solar radiation at a rate of $8.2 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~cm}^{-2} \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$. If the sun radiates as the black bodies, the temperature at the surface of the sun will be (the angle subtended by sun on the earth in suppose $0.53^{\circ}$ and Stefan constant is $\sigma=5.67 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{Wm}^{-2} \mathrm{~K}^4$ )
questions.solution:
Let diameter of the sun is $d$ while radius of the earth is $r$ then
$\begin{aligned} \frac{D}{2} & \approx 0.53 \times \frac{\pi}{180} \\ & =9.25 \times 10^{-3}\end{aligned}$
The radiation emitted per unit area of the sun is
$4 \pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 \sigma T^A=\pi D^2 \sigma T^A$
The radiation received at the earths surface per unit time per unit area is $\frac{\pi \sigma d T^4}{4 \pi r^2}=\frac{\sigma T^4}{4}\left(\frac{d}{R}\right)^2\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow & & \frac{\sigma T^4}{4}\left(\frac{D}{R}\right)^2 & =82 \mathrm{Jcm}^{-2} \mathrm{~min}^{-1} \\ & \text { or } & \frac{1}{4} \times 5.67 \times 10^{-8} \times T^4 \times\left(9.25 \times 10^{-3}\right)^2 \\ & = & \frac{8.2}{10^{-4} \times 60} \mathrm{Wm}^{-2} \\ \Rightarrow & & T & =5794 \mathrm{~K} \cong 5800 \mathrm{~K}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lead ball at $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is dropped from a height of 6.2 km . The ball is heated due to the air resistance and it completely melts just before reaching the ground. The molten substance falls slowly on the ground. If the specific heat of lead $=126 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-10} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$ and melting point of lead $=130 \quad{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and suppose that any mechanical energy lost is used to heat the ball, then the latent heat of fusion of lead is
questions.solution:
The gravitational potential energy of the ball $=m g h\begin{aligned} & =m \times 10 \times 6.2 \times 10^3 \\ & =m \times 62 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
Now energy required to take ball from $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $330^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is
$m \times 126 \times 300=m \times 37800$
Energy required to melt the ball $=mL$ 
where, $L=$ latent heat
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow m \times 6.2 \times 10^4 \times L & =m \times 37800+mL \\ L & =2.4 \times 10^4 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A slab consists of portions of different materials of same thickness and having the conductivities $K_1$ and $K_2$. The equivalent thermal conductivity of the slab is
questions.solution:
As two portions of the slab are connected in series, therefore
$\begin{aligned} K & =\frac{\sum x_i}{\sum x_i / K_1}=\frac{d+d}{\frac{d}{K_1}+\frac{d}{K_2}} \\ & =\frac{2 d}{d\left(\frac{1}{K_1}+\frac{1}{K_2}\right)}=\frac{2 K_1 K_2}{K_1+K_2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two rigid boxes containing different ideal gases are placed on table. Box A contains one mole of nitrogen at temperature $T_0$, while box $B$ contains 1 mole of helium at temperature $7 / 3 T_0$. The boxes are then put into thermal contact with each other and heat flows between them until the gases reach a common final temperature (ignore the heat capacity of boxes) then the final temperature of gases, $T_f$ in terms of $T_0$ is

questions.q: The temperature of the cold junction of thermocouple is $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and the temperature of hot junction is $T^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The emf is $E=16 T-0.04 T^2 \quad \mu \mathrm{V}$. The inversion temperature $T_i$ is
questions.solution:

$E=16 T-0.04 T^2$
At inversion temperature, $E=0\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad 16 T-0.04 T^2 & =0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad T_i & =\frac{16}{0.04}=400^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A diatomic gas $(\gamma=1.4)$ does 200 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Find the heat given to the gas in the process.
questions.solution:
For a diatomic gas
$C_V=\frac{5}{2} R$ and $C_p=\frac{7}{2} R$
The work done in an isobaric process is
$\begin{aligned} W & =p\left(V_2-V_1\right)=n R\left(T_2-T_1\right) \\ \Rightarrow T_2-T_1 & =\frac{W}{n R}\end{aligned}$
The heat given in an isobaric process is
$\begin{aligned} Q & =n C_p\left(T_2-T_1\right) \\ n C_p \frac{W}{n R} & =\frac{7}{2} W \\ & =\frac{7}{2} \times 200 \mathrm{~J} \\ & =700 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 1 kg of water is converted into steam at the same temperature and at 1 atm ( 100 kPa ). The density of water and steam are $1000 \mathrm{kgm}^{-3}$ and $0.6 \mathrm{kgm}^{-3}$ respectively. The latent heat of vaporisation of water is $2.25 \times 10^6 \mathrm{Jkg}^{-1}$. What will be increase in energy?
questions.solution:
The volume of 1 kg water $=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~m}^3$
and volume of 1 kg steam
$=\frac{1}{0.6} \mathrm{~m}^3$
The increase in volume
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{0.6} \mathrm{~m}^3-\frac{1}{1000} \mathrm{~m}^3 \\ & =(1.7-0.001) \mathrm{m}^3 \\ & \cong 1.7 \mathrm{~m}^3\end{aligned}$
The work done by steam is
$\begin{aligned} W & =(100 \mathrm{kPa})\left(1.7 \mathrm{~m}^3\right) \\ & =1.7 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
The change in intemal energy
$\begin{aligned} \Delta U & =\Delta Q-\Delta W \\ & =2.25 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~J}-1.7 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J} \\ & =208 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For an adiabatic expansion of a mono atomic perfect gas, the volume increases by $24 \%$. What is the percentage decrease in pressure?
questions.solution:
As we know that
$\begin{aligned} p V^\gamma & =K \\ \therefore \Delta p V^\gamma+p \gamma V^{\gamma-1} \Delta V & =0\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{\Delta p}{p}\right)=-\gamma\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$
For monoatomic gas, $\gamma=\frac{5}{3}\therefore \quad \frac{\Delta p}{p}=\frac{5}{3} \times 24 \%=40 \%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The rms speed (in $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ ) of oxygen molecules of the gas at temperature 300 K , is
questions.solution:
The rms speed is given by $v_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M_0}}$
where, $\begin{aligned} R & =\text { gas constant } \\ T & =\text { Temperature of the gas } \\ \text { and } M_0 & =\text { Molecular weight of the gas } \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{3 \times 8.3 \times 300}{32 \times 10^{-3}}} \\ & =483 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A horizontal tube of length $l$ closed at both ends, contains an ideal gas of molecular weight $M$. The tube is rotated at a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about a vertical axis passing through an end. Assuming the temperature to be uniform and constant. If $p_1$ and $p_2$ denote the pressure at free and the fixed end respectively, then choose the correct relation.
questions.solution: Consider the diagram Consider the elemetary part of thickness $d x$ at a distance $x$ from axis of rotation, then force on this part $A d p=(d m) \omega^2 x\ldots$ (i) where, $d m=$ mass of element Now, from ideal gas equation $p V=n R T$ we get $p A d x=\frac{d m}{M} R T\Rightarrow \quad d m=\frac{M p A}{R T} d x$ ...(ii) From Eqs. (i) and (ii) $\begin{aligned} & A d p=\frac{M p A}{R T} \omega^2 x d x \\ & \int_{p_1}^{p_2} \frac{d p}{p}=\int_0^1 \frac{M \omega^2}{R T} x d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \ln \frac{p_2}{p_1}=\frac{M \omega^2 I^2}{2 R T} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{p_2}{p_1}=e^{\frac{M \omega^2 I^2}{2 R T}} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A particle is subjected to two simple harmonic motions along $X$-axis while other is along a line making angle $45^{\circ}$ with the $X$-axis. The two motions are given by $x=x_0 \sin \omega t$ and $s=s_0 \sin \omega t$.
The amplitude of resultant motion is
questions.solution:
Two SHMs are separated at angle $45^{\circ}$. So, resultant amplitude is
$\begin{aligned} & A_R=\sqrt{\left(s_0+x_0 \cos 45^{\circ}\right)^2+\left(x_0 \sin 45^{\circ}\right)^2} \\ & \quad=\sqrt{\left(s_0^2+x_0^2 \cos ^2 45^{\circ}+2 x_0 s_0 \cos 45^{\circ}+x_0^2 \sin ^2 45^{\circ}\right)} \\ & \quad=\sqrt{s_0^2+x_0^2+\sqrt{2} x_0 s_0}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Figure shows spring + block + pulley system which are light. The time period of mass would be
questions.solution:
Let when $m$ is hanging, the extension in the spring is $l$, then tension in the string is,
$T_1=k l=m g$
when force is applied, let the further extension is x . The tension in the spring is
$T_2=k(x+l)\begin{aligned} & \therefore \text { Driving force }=T_2-T_1=k(x+l)-k l=k x \\ & \therefore \text { Acceleration }=\frac{k l}{m}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\text { displacement }}{\text { acceleration }}} \\ & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{x}{\frac{k x}{m}}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 4 kg block is suspended from the ceiling of an elevator through a spring having a linear mass density of $19.2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$. questions.q: Three equal charges, each having a magnitude of $2.0 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$, are placed at the three corners of a right angled triangle of sides $3 \mathrm{~cm}, 4 \mathrm{~cm}$ and 5 cm . The force (in magnitude) on the charge at the right angled corner is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two charges of $+10 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $+20 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are separated by a distance 2 cm . The net potential (electric) due to the pair at the middle point of the line joining the two changes, is
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two small balls, each carrying a charge $q$ are suspended by equal insulator strings of length 1 m from the hook of a stand. This arrangement is carried in a satellite in space. The tension in each string will be
questions.solution:

i.e.,

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Find the resistance of a hollow cylindrical conductor of length 1.0 mm and 2.0 mm respectively. The resistivity of the material is $2.0 \times 10^{-8} \Omega \mathrm{m}$.
questions.solution:
The area of cross-section of the conductor through which charges will be flow is
$\begin{aligned} A & =\pi(20 \mathrm{~mm})^2-\pi(1.0 \mathrm{~mm})^2 \\ & =3 \times \pi \mathrm{mm}^2\end{aligned}$
The resistance of the wire is therefore
$\begin{aligned} R & =\rho \frac{1}{A}=\frac{\left(2.0 \times 10^{-8}\right) \times(10)}{3.0 \times \pi \times 10^{-6}} \\ & =2.1 \times 10^{-3} \Omega\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ammeter shown in figure consists of a $480 \Omega$ coil connected in parallel to a $20 \Omega$ shunt. The reading of ammeter is
questions.solution:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The galvanometer resistance is $30 \Omega$ and it is connected to 2 V battery along with a resistance $2000 \Omega$ in series. A full scale deflection of 25 divisions is obtained. In order to reduce this deflection to 20 divisions, the resistance in series should be
questions.solution:

Current $\quad i=\frac{2}{2030} \mathrm{~A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two long straight wires, each carrying an electric current of 5 A, are kept parallel to each other at a separation of 2.5 cm. Find the magnitude of the magnetic force experiment by 10 cm of a wire.
questions.solution:
The field at the site of one wire due to the other is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The parts of two concentric circular arcs joined by two radial lines and carries current $i$. The arcs subtend an angle $\theta$ at the centre of the circle. The magnetic field at the centre $O$, is
questions.solution:
The field at the centre of a circular loop is given by
$B=\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 a}$
The field due to circular arc of inner circle is
$B_1=\left(\frac{\theta}{2 \pi}\right) \frac{\mu_0 i}{2 a}$
The field due to circular arc of outer circle is
$\begin{aligned} B_2 & =\left(\frac{\theta}{2 \pi}\right)\left(\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 b}\right) \\ B & =B_1-B_2=\frac{\mu_0 i(b-a) \theta}{4 \pi a b}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: The current will be equally divided at junction $P$. questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic flux through each turn of a coil having 200 turns is given as $\left(t^2-2 t\right) \times 10^{-3}$ Wb , where $t$ is in second. The emf induced in the coil at $t=3 \mathrm{~s}$ is
questions.solution:
Given magnetic flux
$\phi=\left(t^2-2 t\right) \times 10^{-3}$
On differentiating with recpect to time $t\frac{d \phi}{d t}=(2 t-2) \times 10^{-3}$
At time $\quad t=3 \mathrm{~s}\begin{aligned}\left|\frac{d \phi}{d t}\right|_{t=3 \mathrm{~s}} & =(2 \times 3-2) \times 10^{-3} \\ & =4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~Wb} \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \\ \text { Now, }|e| & =N\left|\frac{d \phi}{d t}\right| \\ & =200 \times 4 \times 10^{-3} \\ & =800 \times 10^{-3}=0.8 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inductor $(L=20 \mathrm{H})$, a resistor $(R=100 \Omega)$ and a battery $(E=10 \mathrm{~V})$ are connected in series. After a long time, the circuit is short-circuited and then the battery is disconnected. Find the current in the circuit at 1 ms after short circuiting.
questions.solution:
The initial current $i=i_0=\frac{E}{R}=\frac{10}{100}=0.10 \mathrm{~A}$
the time constant, $\tau=\frac{L}{R}=\frac{20 \mathrm{mH}}{100 \Omega}=0.20 \mathrm{~ms}$
The current at $t=1 \mathrm{~ms}$ is
$\begin{aligned} i & =i_0 e^{-t / \tau} \\ & =(0.10) e^{\left(\frac{-1 \mathrm{~ms}}{0.20 \mathrm{~ms}}\right)} \\ & =(0.10) e^5=6.7 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The de-Broglie wavelength of electron falling on the target in an X-ray tube is $\lambda$. The cut-off wavelength of the emitted X-ray is
questions.solution:
The de-Broglie wavelength is given by
$\lambda=\frac{h}{p}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E}}$ ...(i)
where, $E$ is the energy of the electron. The cut-off wavelength $\lambda_0$ is given by
$\lambda_0=\frac{h C}{E}$ ...(ii)
From Eq. (i),
$\lambda^2=\frac{h^2}{2 m E}\Rightarrow \quad E=\frac{h^2}{2 m X^2}$ ... (iii)
Substituting the value of $E$ from Eq. (ii), we get
$\lambda_0=\frac{h c}{\frac{h^2}{2 m \lambda^2}}=\frac{2 m c \lambda^2}{h}$

questions.solution: As we know that time period, $T=\frac{2 \pi r}{V}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad T & =2 \pi \times \frac{h^2}{4 \pi m e^2} \times \frac{h}{2 \pi e^2} \\ & =\frac{h^3}{4 \pi^2 m e^4}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \text { Current, } i & =\frac{\text { Charge }(q)}{T} \\ & =\frac{e}{T}=\frac{e}{\frac{h^3}{4 \pi^2 m e^4}} \\ & =\frac{4 \pi^2 m e^5}{h^3}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:

Now average life
$t_{a v}=\frac{1}{\lambda}=3.9$ days

questions.q: A nucleus disintegrates into two nuclear parts which have their velocities in the ratio $2: 1$. The ratio of their nuclear size will be
questions.solution:

But $m=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \rho \text { or } m \propto r^3\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{r_1^3}{r_2^3} \\ \therefore & \frac{r_1^3}{r_2^3}=\frac{V_2}{V_1}=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{r_1}{r_2}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{1 / 3} \\ \therefore & r_1: r_2=1:(2)^{1 / 3}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A change of 8.0 mA in the emitter current brings a change of 7.9 mA in the collector current. The value of $\alpha$ will be
questions.solution:
We have,
$\begin{aligned} \quad I_E & =I_B+I_C \\ \Delta I_E & =\Delta I_B+\Delta I_C\end{aligned}$
According to question,
$\text { Thus, } \quad \begin{aligned}
\Delta I_E & =8.0 \mathrm{~mA} \\
\Delta I_C & =7.9 \mathrm{~mA} \\
\Delta I_B & =8.0 \mathrm{~mA}-7.9 \mathrm{~mA} \\
& =0.1 \mathrm{~mA}
\end{aligned}$
Thus, $\quad \Delta I_B=8.0 \mathrm{~mA}-7.9 \mathrm{~mA}$
Now, $\alpha=\frac{I_C}{I_E}=\frac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta I_E}=\frac{7.9 \mathrm{~mA}}{8.0 \mathrm{~mA}} \cong 0.99$

the reduced pressure, $\pi=\frac{F}{F_C}$ the reduced volume, $\phi=\frac{V}{V_C}$
Thus, it can be said that the reduced equation of state may be given as

What would be the heat released when an aqueous solution containing 0.5 mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ is mixed with 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$?
(enthalpy of neutralisation is -57.1 kJ )

Thus, 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions will combine with 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions to form 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ and 0.2 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions will remain unreacted. Therefore, heat evolved wher 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions combine with 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions $=0.3 \times 57.1=17.13 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

\text{D.} & \text{Inhibitory ratio} & 4. & 13: 3 \\
\hline
\end{array}$
Codes
questions.solution:
Epistasis is interaction between two or more genes to control a single phenotype. Dominant epistasis also called masking has a ratio $12: 3: 1$ in the $\mathrm{F}_2$ phenotype. Supplementary genes which is recessive epistasis has ratio $9: 3: 4$.
Complementary gene where both dominant alleles are needed for phenotype has ratio 9:7. Inhibitor gene where one gene inhibits the expression of another gene has ratio $13: 3$ in $\mathrm{F}_2$ progeny.
